conventions.convention: For d ≥ 1, Hermitian d-by-d matrices form a real vector space with pairing Tr(AB), norm sqrt(Tr(A²)), synthesis S c = Σa c_a F_a, and Gram entries G_ab = Tr(F_a F_b). Informational completeness means spanning this entire real vector space.

G⁺ is the unique real Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse satisfying the four Penrose equations; canonical duals use D_a = Σb (G⁺)_ba F_b. Redundant spanning families and singular Gram matrices are permitted.

An instrument has finitely many completely positive maps between finite matrix spaces whose sum preserves trace. The dilation orders output space before register space; partial trace removes the register. Zero outcome maps have empty Kraus families and zero register projections.

The joint-measurability equivalence concerns two finite projection-valued measures, each with pairwise orthogonal projections summing to identity. It is not a commutation criterion for arbitrary POVMs.

The tomography procedure accepts nonnegative frequencies summing to one and returns linear inversion without projection onto the positive cone. The stability theorem explicitly extends its output formula to all real vectors.

Sampling uses n ≥ 1 independent categorical trials with the stated product law, and 0 < δ < 1. Independence across different outcome indicators within a trial is neither assumed nor used. The probability bounds are conditional mathematical conclusions, not reported empirical results.
Bernoulli parameters include p = 0 and p = 1; the two-sided bound holds for every t > 0 under the explicitly specified finite product law, without an axiom-of-choice assumption.

load_bearing.statement: For d,m ≥ 1 and a real spanning family F_1,…,F_m in H_d, the Gram pseudoinverse has spectral formula G⁺ = Σλ>0 λ⁻¹P_λ, and every X ∈ H_d satisfies X = Σa Tr(XF_a)D_a. Redundant families are allowed; G need not be invertible.

The pairing Tr(AB) is a real inner product on H_d, with norm sqrt(Tr(A²)). For every finite Hermitian family its Gram matrix is real symmetric positive semidefinite, equals S* S, and satisfies ker G = ker S.

For a spanning finite POVM and density matrix ρ, X(p) = ρ and every f ∈ R^m satisfies ‖X(f)−ρ‖HS ≤ ‖D‖2→HS ‖f−p‖2. Under the specified independent categorical product law, with probability at least 1−δ, max_a |f_a−p_a| ≤ sqrt(log(2m/δ)/(2n)), and consequently ‖X(f)−ρ‖HS ≤ ‖D‖2→HS sqrt(m) sqrt(log(2m/δ)/(2n)).
For n ≥ 1 independent Bernoulli(p) variables with the specified product law, p ∈ [0,1], their frequency f satisfies P(|f−p| ≥ t) ≤ 2 exp(−2nt²) for every t > 0. No axiom of choice is assumed.

Every finite nonempty family of completely positive maps I_a:M_d(C)→M_e(C), d,e ≥ 1, whose sum preserves trace admits q ≥ 1, an isometry V:C^d→C^e⊗C^q, and pairwise orthogonal register projections Q_a summing to identity such that I_a(X) = Tr_E[(I_e⊗Q_a)VXV*(I_e⊗Q_a)] for every input matrix X.

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite Hermitian spectral decomposition, positive square roots, density-matrix calculus, and real Gram spectral reconstruction.
Trace cyclicity in establishing the real Hermitian pairing and the synthesis-adjoint coordinate formula.
The Hilbert–Schmidt triangle inequality and finite bounds establishing the induced reconstruction norm.
The four Penrose equations defining the real Gram pseudoinverse.
Existence and uniqueness of G⁺ and identification of the constructed spectral inverse with G⁺.
The centered unit-interval exponential-moment bound used in the local Bernoulli concentration proof.
Exact finite-dimensional definitions of complete positivity and trace preservation in instrument dilation.
Finite Kraus representations, empty representations for zero maps, complete positivity of Kraus maps, and the trace-preserving normalization criterion.
Effects, POVMs, normalized Kraus instruments, outcome probabilities, and update maps in compatibility, tomography, and the disturbance counterexample.
Existence of the supremum defining the finite induced reconstruction norm after proving nonemptiness and boundedness.
